adhd.label: Step 1 · Jumps to Ch. 4: The General Formula for Capital M–C–M' (Start Here)
adhd.brief: Instead of getting bogged down in Ch. 1's 20 yards of linen, we start at Ch. 4 where Marx makes the mechanism crystal clear: ordinary people sell goods to buy what they need (C–M–C), whereas capital spends money only to end up with more money (M–C–M').

adhd.label: Step 2 · Jumps Back to Ch. 1, Sec. 4: The Fetishism of Commodities
adhd.brief: Now jumps back to the famous section of Chapter 1 where Marx shows how market price tags disguise human relationships between workers as magical properties of things.

adhd.label: Step 3 · Jumps to Part VIII: So-Called Primitive Accumulation
adhd.brief: Jumps to the vivid historical narrative at the end of Volume I, tracing how land enclosures, colonial trade, and national debt forged the modern capitalist system.
